title: Cubic lower-bound inequality for 3-query locally decodable codes
statement:
Let $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 2$ be integers, and let $\delta, \varepsilon \in (0,1]$. Suppose $L$ is a normal form $(3,\delta,\varepsilon)$-decodable code with message length $k$ and block length $n$, whose density parameter equals $\delta$ and whose advantage parameter equals $\varepsilon$. Then there exists a real constant $C > 0$ for which
\[
  k^3 \;\le\; \frac{n \, C \, (\log n)^6}{\varepsilon^{16}\,\delta^{16}} .
\]
Here $C$ is quantified after $k$, $n$, $\delta$, $\varepsilon$ and the code $L$ have been fixed, so it is permitted to depend on all of them.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a normal form $(3,\delta,\varepsilon)$-decodable code with message length $k$ and block length $n$
conclusion: existence of a constant $C > 0$, quantified after all parameters, with the stated inequality
caveat: The Lean places the existential for $C$ inside the conclusion, after every parameter is fixed, so the informalization reflects that $C$ may depend on $k, n, \delta, \varepsilon$ and $L$; I have rendered this faithfully rather than as an absolute constant.
replaced:
Let $k > 0$, $n \ge 2$, and let $\delta, \varepsilon \in (0,1]$. Let $L$ be a normal form
$(3,\delta,\varepsilon)$-decodable code with message length $k$ and block length $n$,
whose parameters are $\delta$ and $\varepsilon$. Then there is a constant $C > 0$ with
\[
  k^3 \;\le\; \frac{n \cdot C \cdot (\log n)^6}{\varepsilon^{16}\,\delta^{16}} .
\]
\emph{Placeholder --- the statement carries no lower-bound content.}  The constant $C$ is
quantified \emph{after} $k$, $n$, $\delta$, $\varepsilon$ and the code $L$, so it may depend on
all of them; the Lean proof takes
$C = (k^3\varepsilon^{16}\delta^{16} + 1)/(n\log^6 n)$, which satisfies the displayed
inequality for \emph{every} choice of parameters.  The intended Theorem~9.1 of
Alrabiah--Guruswami--Kothari--Manohar requires an \emph{absolute} $C$, quantified before the
instance, and would yield $n = \Omega(k^3/\log^6 k)$; that theorem is \emph{not} formalised
here, and this entry must not be cited as a formalisation of it.
